   DISCUSSION ITEM

1.  SUBJECT:  JOINT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THE IMPACTS OF THE LACK OF
  AFFORDABLE HOUSING IN SAN DIEGO AND DECLARING INTENT
  TO WORK TOGETHER TO SUPPORT INCREASING THE REGION’S
  AFFORDABLE HOUSING SUPPLY (DISTRICTS: ALL)
  OVERVIEW
  The County Board of Supervisors (Board) and San Diego City Council (City Council) are coming
  together to jointly acknowledge and address the region’s top issue: the affordable housing crisis. The
  lack of affordable housing in our region is negatively impacting our economic growth and is the primary
  driver of our homelessness problem. The County and the City will commit to working together on
  innovative and practical steps to help us realize 10,000 new units of affordable housing by 2030.

  Today’s Board action will express and acknowledge the sense of the Board that a lack of affordable
  housing is the primary driver of our homelessness crisis and further represents the greatest risk to the
  long-term economic health and prosperity of the region, and that the Board will support collaborative
  efforts with the City Council to increase the supply of affordable housing to meet and exceed the goal
  of 10,000 new units of affordable housing by 2030.

  RECOMMENDATION(S)
  CHAIR NATHAN FLETCHER
  Adopt joint resolution, to the extent legally permissible by the body’s respective authority and
  jurisdiction, that the lack of affordable housing is the primary driver of our homelessness crisis and
  further represents the greatest risk to the long-term economic health and prosperity of the region. The
  body will jointly resolve to continuing to work together to support increasing the supply of affordable
  housing to meet and exceed the goal of 10,000 new units of affordable housing by 2030.

  EQUITY IMPACT STATEMENT
  The region’s affordable housing crisis has only gotten worse since the pandemic with those at the
  lowest end of the economic spectrum most adversely impacted. Recent studies have found that Black
  renters in San Diego are the most burdened by rent and spend 18% more of their income on rent
  compared to Black households nationally. Homeownership rates among Whites still far outpace
  homeownership rates among Latinos and Black households, and as the region’s affordable housing
  crisis intensifies, it exacerbates racial wealth gaps.

  SUSTAINABILITY IMPACT STATEMENT
  This resolution aims to promote sustainable growth and ensure alignment with climate goals set by state
  and federal law.

  FISCAL IMPACT
  There are no direct expenditures being authorized by the Board of Supervisors through this action. At
  this time, there will be no change in net General Fund cost and no additional staff years.
  There may be future fiscal impacts based on recommendations from today’s action. Funding for the

Monday, October 3, 2022  3
   costs will need to be identified; Departments will monitor their budgets and return to the Board with
  mid-year action to adjust the budget as necessary and/or incorporate future budgets as funding
  becomes available. Staff will return to the Board for consideration and approval of any other future
  fiscal impacts that may result from the recommendations. Upon return by staff, funding for future costs
  will need to be identified by the department and will proceed once identified.
  BUSINESS IMPACT STATEMENT
  This resolution will acknowledge the leading role that our housing market is playing in stifling economic
  growth, squeezing middle and working-class families, and fueling the rise of homelessness in our region.
  The cost of this housing affordability crisis is measured in lost productivity when the workers supporting
  our businesses can’t find affordable places to live. This resolution aims to set the foundation for efforts
  to promote increased regional growth.
